raw_case_text: A 16-year-old girl was admitted to the hospital because of abnormal mental behaviour for more than seven months, which had been aggravated for nine days. Seven months previously, the girl developed mental and behavioural abnormalities after a heartbreak, which manifested as alternating low mood and emotional irritability, a lack of interest in social relations, and memory loss. Her parents, brother, and sister were in good health and the parents were nonconsanguineous. There was no family history of genetic diseases. Her parents took her to the local hospital for consultation, but the general physical examination and laboratory test results were normal, and no treatment was administered. A few months later, the patient's symptoms worsened; she refused to eat, drink, sleep, or communicate, exhibited slowness in movement, and was finally transferred to our hospital. The physical examination showed the following results: clear consciousness; able to answer simple questions; and no redness, ulcers or vegetation in the perianal skin. The bilateral Babinski sign and the right Oppenheim sign were positive. No obvious abnormalities were observed on cardiopulmonary or abdominal physical examinations. Tests for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and human immunodeficiency virus were negative. The treponemal serological test result was positive and the toluidine red unheated serum test (TRUST) titre was 1:128. The results of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) testing results are as follows: White blood cells: 5.0 x106/L, Red blood cells: 2.5x106/L, Glucose:3.41 mmol/L, Cl-:128.3 mmol/L, Total protein:970.0 mg/L, Treponema pallidum particle agglutination test (TPPA): positive. Brain computed tomography (CT) showed a bilateral cerebral hemisphere gray matter junction area, scattered calcification in the bilateral lenticular nucleus and thalamus, bilateral semioval centre, lateral ventricle brain white matter region, a slightly widened and deepened sulcus, and a slightly narrowed frontal parietal gyrus (Figure 1). After admission, the possibility of neurosyphilis infection was considered. The patient was administered an intravenous penicillin G solution, oral olanzapine, and depakin for 12 days. After treatment, the patient's clinical symptoms improved, and she was discharged with her parents. We informed the patient to continue penicillin G treatment at a hospital near their home.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 16-year-old girl presented with a >7-month history of progressive behavioral and psychiatric abnormalities that worsened acutely over the preceding 9 days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Seven months prior to admission, following a romantic breakup, the patient developed alternating low mood, emotional irritability, social withdrawal, and memory loss. Initial evaluation at a local hospital showed normal general physical and basic laboratory findings, and no treatment was given. Over the subsequent months, her condition worsened until 9 days prior to admission when she refused to eat, drink, sleep, or communicate and exhibited marked psychomotor retardation.
subjective.past_medical_history: No prior medical illnesses. Parents were healthy and non-consanguineous, siblings were healthy, and there was no family history of genetic or psychiatric disorders.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for mood lability, irritability, social withdrawal, memory decline, psychomotor slowing, and refusal to eat, drink, sleep, or speak.

objective.physical_examination: On admission, the patient had clear consciousness and could answer simple questions. Cardiopulmonary, abdominal, and perianal skin examinations were normal without ulcers or vegetations. Neurological examination revealed psychomotor slowing, bilateral positive Babinski signs, and a positive right Oppenheim sign.
objective.routine_investigations: Serological screening tests for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Non-contrast brain CT demonstrated hypoattenuation at the bilateral cerebral gray-white matter junctions and semioval centers, scattered calcifications in the bilateral lenticular nuclei and thalami, mildly widened and deepened cerebral sulci, and mild frontoparietal gyral atrophy. Lumbar puncture CSF analysis revealed WBC 5.0 x 10^6/L, RBC 2.5 x 10^6/L, glucose 3.41 mmol/L, chloride 128.3 mmol/L, and markedly elevated total protein of 970.0 mg/L.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed parenchymatous neurosyphilis presenting with psychiatric and cognitive manifestations in an adolescent, established via positive serum treponemal serology, high-titer serum TRUST (1:128), and positive CSF TPPA alongside elevated CSF protein (970.0 mg/L). Treated with intravenous penicillin G, oral olanzapine, and oral valproate (Depakine) for 12 days with clinical improvement, and discharged to complete her intravenous penicillin G course at a local hospital.
